messages.subject_clean: Build Index has a long time
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I have started a build index at June, 04@12:00PM. To day is June, 06@9:00AM. Elapsed 45 hours and it not finished yet. It is running in a Debian Testing box in a Dell Inspiron Core i7 with 8 GB of RAM. I was building index from Eucalyptus grandis genome (~700 MB). This time is ok or something have occurred? I was running R inside Emacs. Have you an estimated time to do so?

Thank you very much!

Marcelo

messages.subject: Re: Build Index has a long time
messages.subject_clean: Build Index has a long time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcelo,

I'm not sure which version of Rsubread that you're using. If it is a recent version, the default setting is to build a full index, and 8GB of memory (and I guess that the available memory size is even smaller if other programs are running) is a little inadequate to that end.

If you're building a full index, you can try to specify "gappedIndex=TRUE" to the index builder; it will substantially reduce memory use for building the index and for mapping the reads.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: multi-overlap versus multi-mapping in featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to confirm my understanding of multi-overlapping versus multi-mapping reads as it pertains to featureCounts. There is the option allowMultiOverlap. This does NOT refer to multi-mapping but rather means that a read maps to a particular location that overlaps with two features (exons) or meta-features (genes), correct? To overlap with two meta-features, the two meta-features would need to be adjacent, partially overlap or fully overlap (one meta-feature fully inside the other meta-feature, for example there are lncRNAs located fully inside protein-coding genes).

Then assume that we set largestOverlap=TRUE. That means that if a read maps to a location that overlaps two (adjacent or overlapping) features or meta-features, it will be assigned to the one it has the larger overlap with (it will only not count if it overlaps both (meta-)features equally).

For example, I am looking at protein-coding genes and their cis-located lncRNAs. In some cases, a (shorter) lncRNA is fully located inside a protein-coding gene. Both of them have non-zero read counts. Based on the above the lncRNA must have a zero read count because any read mapping to the protein-coding gene would either have a larger overlap with the protein-coding gene or the overlap would be the same and the read would not count. So the non-zero read count for the lncRNA must come from it having introns which the protein-coding gene does not.

Lastly I set countMultiMappingReads = FALSE as recommend so that reads mapping to multiple locations do not get counted. This would get overridden by primaryOnly=TRUE but I leave it at FALSE and do not know why one would set it to TRUE?

Does all of the above make sense? Thank you - Ina

messages.subject: Re: multi-overlap versus multi-mapping in featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ina,

Most of your understanding is correct. However I just want to clarify the following two scenarios:
(1) When largestOverlap and allowMultiOverlap are both set to TRUE and there are two or more features that have the same largest overlap with the read, this read will be counted to all these features.
(2) The primaryOnly option does not override countMultiMappingReads option. When countMultiMappingReads is set to FALSE, no multi-mapping reads will be counted. Their primary and secondary alignments will all be ignored.

Best
Wei

messages.subject_clean: Some genes have no counts (empty) in featurecounts table
messages.body_plain:
Hi Prof. Shi,
I got a issue that some transposon expressions were reported with empty counts (no counts), see sheet1 in the enclosed file, when I used featurecounts to count the reads. Here is my code:

featureCounts -T 24 -t exon -g gene_id -a /mm10_UCSC_rmsk_190619.gtf -o ./fast/PIWIsc.TE/count/TE_GeneLevel_counts.txt /fast/PIWIsc.TE/bam.align/*.bam

The version of featureCounts is v1.6.0. There is no error massage.
I noticed that transposons (like genes) with empty counts have more than 6552 exons, see the number of chr in sheet2 in enclosed file. Is there a limit in the number of exons that featureCounts would count? How can I overcome this issue?
I downloaded .gtf file generated by repeatmasker from UCSC.

Best,
Mingxing Yang
